newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain responds to UN query on Rwanda arms shipment.
newsitem.headline: Spain responds to UN query on Rwanda arms shipment.

text.p: Spain has informed the United Nations that a plane which left from Madrid in 1994 and is under investigation for shipping arms to Rwanda carried only food, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Sunday.

A U.N. commission investigating arms shipments to the region during the conflict two years ago raised questions in a report released on Tuesday about the May 1994 flight said to have been carrying arms bound for exiled Rwandan Hutus.
The Nigerian-registered plane left from Madrid and stopped in Malta before going on to eastern Zaire, according to the report. It carried 30 tonnes of weapons, the report said.
"...The worst thing carried in the cargo hold was food products," spokesman Jose Luis Solano said. He said the Boeing B707 aircraft had made a "technical stopover" in Madrid for a few weeks.

The commission said on Tuesday it had not received an answer from Spain in response to a request for the information. Solano said the Spanish consulate in New York had answered a query about the flight three weeks ago.

The U.N. commission is trying to uncover the activities of former Rwandan army colonel Theoneste Bagosera, who ordered weapons for exiled Hutus in complicity with Zairean officials, according to the report.

Bagosera has been accused of playing a central role in the 1994 genocide of one million Rwandan Tutsis and of trying to re-arm the exiled resistance to the Tutsi-led force that became the present Rwandan government.
Bagosera is believed to have boarded the plane in question in Malta. The shipment was made a month after the massacres of minority Rwandan Tutsis had begun.
In the armed conflict that followed, defeated Hutu forces were setting up bases in or near Zaire, the commission said.
Bagosera is now in jail in Cameroon after Belgium requested his detention and extradition on charges that he killed 10 Belgian U.N. peacekeepers based in Rwanda in April 1994.
